name: Metropolia University of Applied Sciences
summary: Applied-sciences university in Helsinki, Espoo and Vantaa; 21 practical English bachelor's, from nursing and robotics to game design.

ib.text: Most programmes select by the International UAS Exam; ten also keep 10–30% of places for certificate-based selection, where IB grades count. Culture degrees use a pre-assignment and own exam.

programmes.name: International Business and Analytics
programmes.about: International business with a focus on data analytics, taught through interactive lectures, field projects and real business cases at the Myllypuro campus in Helsinki.
programmes.overview: You study finance, accounting, marketing, supply chain management and international business, with a professional major in Business Analytics and electives such as human resources and strategic management. Sustainability reporting, corporate responsibility and innovation projects run through the curriculum. Teaching uses interactive lectures, company field trips, real business cases and multidisciplinary projects with other Metropolia programmes and companies, followed by a work placement and a thesis. Exchange is possible at over 60 partner universities. Graduates work as data analysts, business analysts, digital transformation specialists and sustainability reporting specialists.
programmes.ib: UAS Exam (50% of places), plus a certificate-based quota for IB holders (30% of places).
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027) for 50% of places; 30% go on certificates such as the IB, ranked with the UAS scoring table.

programmes.name: International Business and Logistics
programmes.about: Supply chain management and marketing studied through interactive lectures, business simulation games and real projects, building strategic thinking for international business.
programmes.overview: You study supply chain management and the operations of international trade, and choose a professional major in either Supply Chain Management or Marketing, with electives in finance, human resources and strategic management. Teaching combines interactive lectures, business simulation games, company field trips, real cases and projects, together with a work placement and a thesis. Exchange studies are possible at over 60 partner universities, and a double degree with HTW Saar in Germany gives you two bachelor's degrees. Graduates work as procurement specialists, logistics coordinators, supply chain analysts, marketing managers and entrepreneurs, or continue to a master's in Finland or abroad.
programmes.ib: UAS Exam (50% of places), plus a certificate-based quota for IB holders (30% of places).
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027) for 50% of places; 30% go on certificates such as the IB, ranked with the UAS scoring table.

separateFrom.name: International Business and Analytics
separateFrom.reason: A different subject: supply chains and marketing, where the other is data analytics; each is its own application.

programmes.name: 3D Game Art
programmes.about: 3D graphics for images, animation, visual effects and real-time applications, including VR/AR/XR, alongside 2D motion graphics, fine art and visual design, at the Arabia campus.
programmes.overview: You learn to use 3D graphics to produce images, animations, special effects and real-time applications, alongside 2D motion graphics, traditional visual arts and visual design, with character design, animation, VFX and compositing as core areas. Teaching is learning by doing: practical exercises and production groups that imitate workplace practice, large collaborative projects, and final-stage work often done with representatives from the industry. The programme is based on the Arabia campus, a creative district of Helsinki. Graduates work as 3D animators, character designers, VFX artists and architectural or product visualisers in games, film and television, advertising and design agencies.
programmes.ib: Pre-assignment by 21 January 2027, then the programme's own entrance exam; IB grades do not decide. Offered in English for the first time in 2027.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-assignment due 21 Jan 2027, 15:00; the top 60 sit an online entrance exam with an interview in week 15 (April). IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Game Design
programmes.about: Designing and producing games: visual design, interactive storytelling and game mechanics, with hands-on work in game engines, extended reality and AI tools.
programmes.overview: You learn to design and produce games in collaborative development teams, covering visual design, interactive storytelling, game mechanics, 3D graphics, virtual environments, character design, programming, AI technologies and extended reality. Teaching happens in production teams that simulate real industry environments, with client-based projects and studio work in industry-standard game engines and 3D software, in an intensive full-time model. The programme builds on Metropolia's earlier XR design education and encourages responsible use of AI. Graduates work in game development, interactive media, simulation, entertainment and digital storytelling, in game studios, design agencies, marketing and educational content.
programmes.ib: Pre-assignment by 21 January 2027, then the programme's own entrance exam; IB grades do not decide. New in 2027.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-assignment due 21 Jan 2027, 15:00; the top 55 sit an online entrance exam with an interview in week 16 (April). IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Sustainable Fashion Business Management
programmes.about: Business for a more responsible fashion industry: brand strategy, consumer behaviour and data-driven decisions for profitable, sustainable fashion companies.
programmes.overview: You study international fashion business, branding and fashion communication, consumer behaviour and trend forecasting, product and merchandising development, and the use of data and technology in business, with sustainability throughout. The programme approaches business specifically from the perspective of the fashion and textile industry, including its global supply chains. Teaching is work-integrated, with projects, collaboration with industry partners and assignments tied to real working life. Graduates work as fashion business specialists, brand development experts, sustainability coordinators, merchandising managers, trend analysts and marketing specialists, or as entrepreneurs.
programmes.ib: Pre-assignment by 21 January 2027, then the programme's own entrance exam; IB grades do not decide. New in 2027.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-assignment due 21 Jan 2027, 15:00; the top 60 sit an online exam (writing, maths reasoning, interview) on 13–14 April 2027. IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Civil Engineering and Building Services
programmes.about: A four-year engineering degree in which you specialise, from the second year, in either civil engineering or building services (HVAC) engineering.
programmes.overview: You study the broad foundations of construction and building services, with a major subject in civil engineering or building services, and develop problem-solving, mathematical and economic thinking, teamwork, IT and communication skills, with sustainable development and digital literacy as themes. Learning is by doing, through problem-solving and cooperation, with a practical work training period and a bachelor's thesis; classes are by day at the Myllypuro campus, and international students learn Finnish alongside engineering. Graduates work as civil or HVAC engineers in engineering and design firms, construction companies, the building products industry, public administration and research institutes.
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam only (23 Mar 2027; pre-identify 10–12 Mar): all places go on the exam, so IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Electronics
programmes.about: Analysing, designing and building electronic systems for communications, consumer electronics, medical devices and automation, including wireless sensor systems.
programmes.overview: The degree starts from the fundamentals of electronics, with the physics and mathematical analysis behind them, and builds toward options in embedded systems design, sensor technologies, radio technology, wireless communications, and electronics design and testing, alongside project management, sustainable development and communication skills. The first two years lean on theory and the later years on applied project work, with a large amount of practical exercises and projects. Study is on the Myyrmaki campus in Vantaa. Graduates work as design and technical specialists, application engineers, technical sales and project managers in communications, consumer electronics, medical devices and automation.
programmes.ib: UAS Exam (80% of places), plus a certificate-based quota for IB holders (10% of places).
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027) for 80% of places; 10% go on certificates such as the IB, ranked with the UAS scoring table.

programmes.name: Information Technology
programmes.about: Core engineering, maths and natural sciences with a strong software-engineering focus, learned through substantial coding projects and real applications.
programmes.overview: After orientation studies you choose a major in Software Engineering, with paths in software, game, mobile or web development covering programming, databases, machine learning and cybersecurity, or in Smart IoT Systems, which focuses on designing, building and securing IoT devices and networks. Mathematics, physics and English support the core, and every course has a substantial coding component with a major project each semester. The study model is intensive and full-time on campus, with industry projects, a work placement and a final year project. Graduates work as software engineers, game, mobile and web developers, or in product development and technical support, and many continue to a master's.
programmes.ib: International UAS Exam. Karamalmi campus, Espoo; Metropolia says the campus may change with its reorganisation from 2026.
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam only (23 Mar 2027; pre-identify 10–12 Mar): all places go on the exam, so IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.about: Mechanical engineering with an eye on sustainable, high-tech solutions, combining strong maths and science with a practical, learning-by-doing approach.
programmes.overview: You build mathematical and scientific foundations and apply them in practical engineering, then choose a major in Machine Design, which covers product development, materials, manufacturing and computer-aided design, or in Aircraft Engineering, which covers aeronautics, aeromechanics, structures, avionics, engines and drones. Theory is combined with practical projects and a work placement that can be partly or fully abroad, followed by a thesis, and international exchange is part of the programme. Finnish language support helps with life and networking in Finland. The Myyrmaki campus in Vantaa hosts the programme, and graduates move into industry or on to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam only (23 Mar 2027; pre-identify 10–12 Mar): all places go on the exam, so IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Robotics Engineering
programmes.about: Robotics engineering on a base of maths and science, learned by doing, with specialisations such as industrial robots, autonomous systems and drones, and industry placements.
programmes.overview: You study robot software, mechatronics, robotics systems, robot perception, and robot control and learning, supported by mathematics, automation, artificial intelligence and mechanical engineering, with entrepreneurship and AI as themes across the degree. The blended format mixes periodic classroom days, small group work, online teaching and independent study, so it can be done alongside work. You learn by doing, take part in Metropolia's research and development innovation hubs, and do excursions, work placements and thesis projects with local and multinational companies. Graduates work as robotics, automation, project and design engineers and technical sales engineers in manufacturing, healthcare, agriculture, logistics and aerospace.
programmes.ib: UAS Exam (80% of places), plus a certificate-based quota for IB holders (10% of places).
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027) for 80% of places; 10% go on certificates such as the IB, ranked with the UAS scoring table.

programmes.name: Smart Automation
programmes.about: Developing and managing smart systems across industries: automation and robotics for manufacturing, production lines and smart factories.
programmes.overview: You study electronics, programming, computer science and electrical engineering, with cyber-physical systems, digital twins and AI and machine learning for automation, combining mechanical and electrical thinking. Real-world projects with Finnish companies let you work on industry challenges, and the skill set reaches beyond software into smart manufacturing, sustainable energy systems, intelligent logistics and smart healthcare. The programme is based at the Myyrmaki campus in Vantaa and prepares you for Industry 5.0 and digitalisation. Graduates work as automation engineers, IoT developers, machine learning engineers, control engineers, smart manufacturing specialists and AI and automation consultants.
programmes.ib: UAS Exam (80% of places), plus a certificate-based quota for IB holders (10% of places).
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027) for 80% of places; 10% go on certificates such as the IB, ranked with the UAS scoring table.

programmes.name: Construction Site Management
programmes.about: Training to lead construction sites: planning and managing site work and supervising construction professionals as a site manager.
programmes.overview: The programme trains you to lead construction work as a site manager, with basic studies in mathematics, sciences and languages, vocational studies in construction and a specialisation in house construction. You learn to plan and run a construction site and to supervise construction professionals. Classes are by day and taught in English and Finnish, with an innovation project commissioned by a company in the field, a work placement and a thesis. The degree meets the legal competence requirements for site management in Finland. Graduates work as site managers or in expert roles in construction services, customer service and property management.
programmes.ib: UAS Exam (80% of places), plus a certificate-based quota for IB holders (10% of places).
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027) for 80% of places; 10% go on certificates such as the IB, ranked with the UAS scoring table.

programmes.name: Laboratory Science
programmes.about: Biological and chemical analysis with advanced laboratory techniques; at least half of the studies take place in the laboratory.
programmes.overview: You learn chemical and biological laboratory methods applied to food safety, water and air quality, forensics, quality assurance, detection of disease-causing microbes and instrumental analysis, with electives in sustainability, programming, leadership, procurement or languages. About half of the contact teaching takes place in well-equipped laboratories, and project work with external partners complements it. A five-month internship in a company or research institute and a thesis done with a partner organisation complete the degree. Graduates work as laboratory analysts, quality specialists, researchers and validation specialists, or continue to a university master's in chemistry or biology.
programmes.ib: UAS Exam (80% of places), plus a certificate-based quota for IB holders (10% of places).
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027) for 80% of places; 10% go on certificates such as the IB, ranked with the UAS scoring table.

programmes.name: Applied Gerontology
programmes.credential: Bachelor of Social Services and Health Care
programmes.about: Work with older people and elderly care: memory work, digital competence and coordinating gerontological care to help older adults live meaningful lives.
programmes.overview: You study the foundations of gerontological expertise, the right to individual ageing, supporting a good life for older people, older people in the home environment, promoting participation and wellbeing, and person-centred guidance. The degree combines campus teaching, independent online study, projects with working-life partners and practical training in real work settings, with Finnish learned along the way. It is taught mainly in English and aimed at international students and immigrants who want a career in Finland. Graduates work as gerontology specialists, social and client counsellors, home care coordinators and service advisers in the public, private and non-profit sectors.
programmes.ib: UAS Exam (70% of places), plus a certificate-based quota for IB holders (10% of places).
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027) for 70% of places; 10% go on certificates such as the IB, ranked with the UAS scoring table.

programmes.name: Biomedical Laboratory Science
programmes.about: Training as a biomedical laboratory scientist: sample collection, patient examinations and laboratory analyses, with quality management and new tools such as AI and genomics.
programmes.overview: You study taking samples, point-of-care testing, clinical histology and cytology, clinical chemistry and haematology, microbiology, genetics, physiology, neurophysiology and nuclear medicine, building laboratory technique and understanding of human cell biology. The degree combines professional studies, hands-on laboratory training, group work, virtual learning and Finnish language courses, with internships spread across the programme, some in the school's own laboratory, and a thesis that can be done with a working-life partner. It is taught mainly in English and designed for international students. Graduates work in hospitals, research laboratories and diagnostic centres, where Finnish is needed for employment.
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam only (23 Mar 2027; pre-identify 10–12 Mar): all places go on the exam, so IB grades do not count.

separateFrom.name: Laboratory Science
separateFrom.reason: A different degree (Bachelor of Health Care, not Laboratory Services) that trains biomedical laboratory scientists, selected on the UAS Exam alone.

programmes.name: Nursing
programmes.about: A bilingual nursing degree taught in English with Finnish built in (none needed at the start); about a third of it is clinical practice with patients.
programmes.overview: You learn clinical nursing skills, communication and decision-making, teamwork in multiprofessional groups and how to organise your work, with professional Finnish language developed step by step alongside. Teaching combines theory, clinical skills training and simulation in a simulation hospital with emergency, intensive care, surgical and paediatric environments, with contact teaching on campus. The bilingual programme is designed for immigrants who start from basic Finnish and study together with Finnish speakers. Graduates become registered nurses working in hospital wards, emergency, intensive care, home care, private health services and health technology, or continue to a master's in advanced practice nursing or nursing science.
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam only (23 Mar 2027; pre-identify 10–12 Mar): all places go on the exam, so IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Occupational Therapy
programmes.about: Occupational therapy learned by alternating theory and practice, mixing campus teaching, online learning and practical training linked to working life.
programmes.overview: You study occupational therapy, health and rehabilitation, how daily activities affect health, assessing participation in everyday life and applying client-centred methods, with work-life projects and a bachelor's thesis. Teaching is blended, combining campus sessions, live online classes, independent study and group work, with practical training in real work environments over four semesters and a personal study plan. The programme stresses evidence-based practice and working with other professions, and Finnish learning is encouraged to support placements. Graduates work in health care and rehabilitation, schools and early childhood education, mental health, occupational health and community organisations.
programmes.ib: UAS Exam (70% of places), plus a certificate-based quota for IB holders (10% of places).
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027) for 70% of places; 10% go on certificates such as the IB, ranked with the UAS scoring table.

programmes.name: Paramedic Nursing
programmes.about: A bilingual degree that qualifies you as both a paramedic and a registered nurse under EU rules, with skills labs, simulations and about a third clinical practice.
programmes.overview: You study emergency care and the treatment of patients of all ages in varied environments, together with general nursing skills and Finnish language studies, so that you qualify as both a paramedic and a registered nurse under EU professional qualification rules. Teaching combines theory, clinical skills labs and simulations in advanced spaces including a simulation hospital and an ambulance, with about a third of the degree in clinical practice with patients, plus innovation studies and a bachelor's thesis. The programme is bilingual, so no prior Finnish is needed to start. Graduates work in ambulances, emergency rooms, intensive care and acute care, or continue to a master's in advanced practice nursing or nursing science.
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam only (23 Mar 2027; pre-identify 10–12 Mar): all places go on the exam, so IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Physiotherapy
programmes.about: Physiotherapy with a holistic, multidisciplinary approach, including applied exercise, aquatic therapy and water rescue training, plus clinical practice.
programmes.overview: You study cooperation and interaction with the client, assessment of functional ability, human body structure and function, biomechanics, motor learning and therapeutic exercise, with applied exercise, aquatic therapy, water rescue training and Finnish language studies throughout. Teaching mixes blended learning, group work, lectures and supervised clinical practice, some in the school's own HyMy Village facilities, and a bachelor's thesis that can be done alone or in small groups with workplace partners. Instruction starts in English and moves toward bilingual delivery. Graduates qualify as licensed physiotherapists and work in hospitals, health centres, private wellbeing and rehabilitation services, or as entrepreneurs.
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam only (23 Mar 2027; pre-identify 10–12 Mar): all places go on the exam, so IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Public Health Nursing
programmes.about: A bilingual degree qualifying you as both a public health nurse and a registered nurse, for primary care and health promotion; no Finnish needed at the start.
programmes.overview: You qualify as both a public health nurse and a registered nurse, studying through theory lessons, practice in skills labs, simulation exercises, language studies and a bachelor's thesis, with Finnish taught from the first semester. About a third of the degree is real healthcare placements, and training uses simulation spaces including a simulation hospital and the HyMy Village. Teaching is bilingual, mainly in English, with international projects and exchange opportunities. Graduates work with people of all ages in maternity clinics, school health services, occupational health, primary care, home care and hospitals, or continue to master's studies in advanced practice nursing or nursing science.
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam only (23 Mar 2027; pre-identify 10–12 Mar): all places go on the exam, so IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Social Services
programmes.about: Socio-pedagogical social work: analysing social issues and their effect on well-being, and working with people of all ages in their everyday environments.
programmes.overview: The degree is built on a social pedagogical approach: empowering citizens, preventing marginalisation and promoting inclusion. It develops five areas of competence, which are ethics in social work, client work, knowledge of social service systems, critical and inclusive citizenship, and research and development skills. Teaching uses lectures, group work, workshops, projects, e-learning and three to four internships in different social service settings, and an early childhood education specialisation is an option. It is taught mainly in English while you learn Finnish. Graduates work in child welfare, family work, youth guidance, school counselling, elderly care, disability services, mental health and substance abuse work.
programmes.ib: UAS Exam (70% of places), plus a certificate-based quota for IB holders (10% of places).
programmes.selectionNote: International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027) for 70% of places; 10% go on certificates such as the IB, ranked with the UAS scoring table.

notes: Several health programmes are taught in English and Finnish together, and Finnish is built into the degree so you can work in Finland afterwards.
Metropolia has not yet published its 2027 deadlines for IB predicted or final grades; Studyinfo.fi will show them.
Metropolia's separate rolling application (1 December to 31 March) is for SAT/ACT and pathway students, not a route on IB grades.
